# Invocation cleanup: freeze marked processes before killing them, and don't start an agent test after its invocation ends

## What happened (2026-10-14)
Two runs ended needs_human with `Invocation termination could not be confirmed: Marked processes still alive: …` (`src/util/proc.ts`, `stopMarkedProcesses`):
- **mv8hblqn0vwehk50p13jah (#533), 15:40.** The Codex implementer's own test built a nested-repository fixture with `submodule.recurse` and a git directory pointing back at the parent. Hundreds of processes were alive when the invocation ended. Load reached 311.
- **mv8gny3y0rh69tr00ql8za (#528's review round), 15:52.** The Claude implementer ran the full suite. It waited 808 s for the gate lane, so Claude's Bash tool moved the command to the background at its 600 s limit. The turn then ended with the suite still running, and about 40 marked processes outlived the cleanup.

`stopMarkedProcesses` signals each marked PID, SIGTERM and then SIGKILL after the grace period, and gives up after the grace period plus 10 s. A tree that keeps forking replaces processes as fast as they are signalled. Under heavy load, scanning and signalling hundreds of processes can also outlast 10 s. Failing closed is right: live writers must not overlap the next step. But the gap between "can't stop them" and "didn't stop them fast enough" costs a run.

## Change
1. **Freeze, then kill.** Each sweep sends SIGSTOP to every marked process it finds, so a stopped process can't fork, and rescans until no unstopped marked process remains. Then it sends SIGKILL to the whole set and confirms it is gone, keeping the PID-reuse checks. The deadline still bounds the whole stop. Refuse only when the frozen set still has live members at the deadline.
2. **Name the cause.** When confirmation still fails, the error names how many processes were alive and their command names, redacted. It should say whether the set kept growing, so "an agent's process tree kept forking" is distinguishable from "the machine was too slow".
3. **Slot waits and Claude's 600 s Bash limit.** A slotted command's wait counts toward Claude Code's per-command limit, so a long wait gets the command moved to the background and the turn ends with it running. Pick one fix, with a test:
   - the wrapper prints a waiting line, so the agent knows to wait instead of moving on; or
   - when an agent invocation ends, an agent test still waiting for a slot exits instead of starting.
   An agent test must never start after its invocation has ended.

## Acceptance
- A fake-harness test fails on today's code: an invocation leaves a process that keeps forking short-lived children. It is stopped within the deadline and the round continues.
- A test: a slotted command still waiting when its invocation ends never starts its command.
- Existing process-cleanup and PID-reuse tests still pass.

Related: #377 (cleanup retries), #150 (overload), #474 (agent test slotting). Budget: about 50 source lines, plus tests.


Closes #537

# Deploy and gate-slot: a busy slot past the 30-minute wait runs the suite unslotted beside factory gates

## What happened (2026-10-15)
- #550's deploy (`limitless deploy --smoke`, which runs its checks inside `withGateLease("deploy", …)` in `src/cli/service.ts`) started waiting for the gate slot at 21:05. At 21:35 the wait hit its 30-minute budget (`maxWaitMs` defaults to 1,800,000 in `src/cli/gate-slot.ts`). `withGateLease` printed `warning: gate-slot coordination unavailable: Error: gate-slot wait passed the acquisition deadline` and ran lint, typecheck and the full suite anyway. That ran from about 21:35 to 21:57, beside the gate that held the slot.
- Two factory gates were running in that window:
  - **#537's regression retry failed again at 21:46** on `change view preserves PR text …`, which timed out at 5037 ms. A retry that fails again counts as a confirmed regression, so the run went back to its implementer for a load timeout.
  - **#545 round 1's test check took 1718 s and failed with 17 timeouts.** They include the baseline-cache, factory-merge-interruption and isolated-push land tests at their 25–30 s limits. Its implementer gets that output as feedback.
- Land 68 (#539) failed later, from 22:16 to 22:39, on 3 timeouts. It did not overlap the deploy, so it is not part of this issue.

## Why
After the wait budget runs out, `withGateLease` treats "the slot is still busy" like "the daemon is unreachable". In both cases it runs the work without the slot. For an unreachable daemon, that is the existing degraded mode, and it's announced. For a healthy daemon with a long queue, it defeats the slot: a second full suite (about 18 minutes here) runs on a machine sized for one, and other runs' gates time out into false regressions. `limitless gate-slot`, which `scripts/land-pr.sh` uses, takes the same path.

## Change
- While the daemon is reachable and answering lease requests, a busy slot never turns into an unslotted run. Keep waiting until the slot is acquired, and print the holder and the elapsed wait every few minutes, so a long wait is visible in the deploy output. Apply this to both `limitless deploy` and `limitless gate-slot`, through the one `withGateLease` path.
- The wait budget still bounds the unreachable-daemon case, which keeps today's fallback and warning.
- The agent-test lanes (#483, #537) keep their current rules.

## Tests (fake lease client and clock, no real daemon)
- A slot that stays busy past `maxWaitMs`, with the daemon answering, doesn't start the work until the slot is acquired. No "coordination unavailable" warning is printed, and progress lines name the holder. This test fails on main today.

# Invocation cleanup: freeze marked processes before killing them, and don't start an agent test after its invocation ends

## What happened (2026-10-14)
Two runs ended needs_human with `Invocation termination could not be confirmed: Marked processes still alive: …` (`src/util/proc.ts`, `stopMarkedProcesses`):
- **mv8hblqn0vwehk50p13jah (#533), 15:40.** The Codex implementer's own test built a nested-repository fixture with `submodule.recurse` and a git directory pointing back at the parent. Hundreds of processes were alive when the invocation ended. Load reached 311.
- **mv8gny3y0rh69tr00ql8za (#528's review round), 15:52.** The Claude implementer ran the full suite. It waited 808 s for the gate lane, so Claude's Bash tool moved the command to the background at its 600 s limit. The turn then ended with the suite still running, and about 40 marked processes outlived the cleanup.

`stopMarkedProcesses` signals each marked PID, SIGTERM and then SIGKILL after the grace period, and gives up after the grace period plus 10 s. A tree that keeps forking replaces processes as fast as they are signalled. Under heavy load, scanning and signalling hundreds of processes can also outlast 10 s. Failing closed is right: live writers must not overlap the next step. But the gap between "can't stop them" and "didn't stop them fast enough" costs a run.

## Change
1. **Freeze, then kill.** Each sweep sends SIGSTOP to every marked process it finds, so a stopped process can't fork, and rescans until no unstopped marked process remains. Then it sends SIGKILL to the whole set and confirms it is gone, keeping the PID-reuse checks. The deadline still bounds the whole stop. Refuse only when the frozen set still has live members at the deadline.
2. **Name the cause.** When confirmation still fails, the error names how many processes were alive and their command names, redacted. It should say whether the set kept growing, so "an agent's process tree kept forking" is distinguishable from "the machine was too slow".
3. **Slot waits and Claude's 600 s Bash limit.** A slotted command's wait counts toward Claude Code's per-command limit, so a long wait gets the command moved to the background and the turn ends with it running. Pick one fix, with a test:
   - the wrapper prints a waiting line, so the agent knows to wait instead of moving on; or
   - when an agent invocation ends, an agent test still waiting for a slot exits instead of starting.
   An agent test must never start after its invocation has ended.

## Acceptance
- A fake-harness test fails on today's code: an invocation leaves a process that keeps forking short-lived children. It is stopped within the deadline and the round continues.
- A test: a slotted command still waiting when its invocation ends never starts its command.
- Existing process-cleanup and PID-reuse tests still pass.

Related: #377 (cleanup retries), #150 (overload), #474 (agent test slotting). Budget: about 50 source lines, plus tests.


Closes #537

Growth comparison ignores the clocks' precision

# Workers: leased gate jobs, the lan executor and the worker loop (#513 slice 2)

The second slice of #513, split out of PR #546 per #513's budget rule ("If it runs over, split the work into two PRs: the listener, pairing, heartbeats and CLI first, then gate jobs, the `lan` executor and the worker loop").

## Scope
Gate jobs, the `lan` gate executor and the worker loop, on top of the first slice (#546: listener, pairing, heartbeats, CLI). The design is #513's. Its acceptance items about leased gate jobs, the `lan` executor and the worker loop move here.

PR #546 at 8562b3d1704bfc0d4746516b254f9e832f8c2ca0 already holds a draft implementation, which this slice can start from:
- `src/gates/lan.ts`;
- the `src/gates/executor.ts`, `src/gates/cache.ts`, `src/pipeline/gate-execution.ts` and `src/pipeline/engine.ts` changes;
- `src/workers/client.ts`;
- their tests in `test/workers.test.ts` and `test/gate-executor.test.ts`.

Budget: about 450 source lines plus tests. Out of scope: as in #513.


The draft commit is in the factory repository cache: read its files with `git show 8562b3d1704bfc0d4746516b254f9e832f8c2ca0:<path>` (start from them, then fit them to what landed in #546 on main).

## #513, the design this slice completes (slice 1 landed as #546)

The budget and scope above are this slice's; #513's text below is the design and acceptance reference. Its items about the listener, pairing, heartbeats and the CLI are already on main.


Part of #165 (M6.2 Throughput), the slice after the executor seam (#482). Matt decided on 2026-10-10 that other machines join as **discovered, as-available workers**, not as a fixed list. This slice builds the worker protocol and a `lan` gate executor on top of the seam. Discovery over Bonjour and availability rules follow in the next slice; here a worker is given the coordinator's URL.

Design reference: docs/research/13-cloud-workers.md §6.2 (executor interface), §3.5 (infrastructure failures).

## Shape
**Workers connect out to the coordinator, the way CI runners do.**
- A worker runs `limitless worker --coordinator https://<host>:<port>`.
- The coordinator never holds a list of machines. It knows only the workers that are paired and sending heartbeats right now.

## Change
1. **A worker listener on the coordinator, off by default.**
   - Configured with `[workers] listen = "<address>:<port>"`.
   - It serves only `/worker/*` routes, separate from the owner API and its port.
   - TLS uses a self-signed certificate generated at first start. Its key is stored as a private file: mode 0600 and read-denied in every agent sandbox, the same way as the API token (#484) and the credential stores (#487).
2. **Pairing.**
   - `limitless worker pair --coordinator <url>` sends the worker's name and its certificate fingerprint.
   - The coordinator records a pending request and shows a short code. The worker prints the same code.
   - The owner approves with `limitless workers approve <code>` (an authenticated owner route), or in the UI.
   - The coordinator then issues a per-worker token and stores only its hash. The worker stores the token and the coordinator's fingerprint, pinned.
   - `limitless workers revoke <name>` ends a worker's access at once.
   - The pairing route only ever creates a pending request. It's rate-limited and grants nothing until approved.
3. **Heartbeats, every 10 s, with the worker's token.** Each carries:
   - the release SHA, bun version, OS and version, CPU count and RAM;
   - free gate slots, whether the machine is on AC power, and idle seconds;
   - the jobs the worker holds.

   The coordinator keeps a `workers` table (additive migration) with each worker's last heartbeat and capabilities. A worker counts as available only while its heartbeats are fresh (30 s).
4. **Version lockstep.** A worker gets jobs only when its release SHA and bun version equal the coordinator's. Otherwise it shows as "needs update" and receives nothing.
5. **Gate jobs** (a `gate_jobs` table: request, state, worker, lease expiry, result).
   - The `lan` executor's `start` enqueues a job and returns `{ kind: "lan", id }`. `attach` waits for the job's result from the store, so a coordinator restart re-attaches without enqueueing again.
   - Workers long-poll `POST /worker/lease` (up to 30 s). A job goes only to a matching, available worker that is asking for work at that moment.
   - Leases expire after 60 s unless renewed by heartbeats.
6. **The worker runs the job.**
   - It fetches `GET /worker/jobs/:id/bundle`, a git bundle of the head (and base) from the coordinator's repository cache, so the worker needs no GitHub credentials. It imports the bundle into its own repository cache through the hardened git wrapper.
   - It checks out exactly the requested head and records `git rev-parse HEAD`.
   - It runs the request's gate config through `runLocalGates`, with its own Seatbelt confinement, scratch and gate slots.
   - It posts check events as they finish, then the `GateRun` and the checked SHA.
   - The worker redacts output with its own registered credentials before sending. Its token and the coordinator's fingerprint are read-denied to its gates.
7. **The coordinator checks the result.**
   - The result is untrusted data. It's validated against the `GateRun` schema, its SHA must equal the requested head, and its checks must be the requested ones.
   - It's redacted again with the coordinator's credentials and private strings before anything stores or shows it.
   - A result that fails any check is an infrastructure failure, never a pass.
8. **Infrastructure failures**:
   - no worker took the job within 60 s;
   - the lease expired;
   - the worker disconnected;
   - the result was invalid.

   These retry once on another available worker, then fall back to the local executor. They are logged as gate events, never sent to the implementer as feedback, and never turn a failing check into a pass. Cancelling the run cancels the job, and the worker stops it on its next heartbeat or lease reply.
9. **Selection.**
   - `[gates] executor = "lan"`, with `[workers] repos = ["owner/name"]` as a per-repository opt-in. Code goes to other machines only for listed repositories.
   - The prepare baseline and the run's gates use the same executor kind. The executor kind joins the baseline cache's environment hash.

## Tests (loopback only, temporary homes, no external network)
Run an in-process coordinator listener and a worker loop over loopback TLS, with certificates generated in temporary directories:
- **Pairing:**
  - an unapproved worker gets no token and no jobs;
  - approval issues a token;
  - revoking a worker refuses its next heartbeat.
- **A job end to end:** the worker leases it, runs real gate commands from a bundle and posts the result. The `GateRun` matches what the local executor gives for the same commit.
- **Restart:** a coordinator restart between `start` and the result re-attaches and doesn't enqueue again.
- **Infrastructure failures:**
  - a worker that stops heartbeating mid-job loses the lease;
  - the job retries once, then runs locally;
  - no implementer feedback is recorded.
- **Bad results:**
  - one whose SHA differs from the request is refused and treated as an infrastructure failure;
  - an extra check, or a check missing from the request, is refused the same way.
- **Version mismatch:** a mismatched worker gets no jobs.
- **Privacy:**
  - the worker's token and the coordinator's TLS key are unreadable from the gate sandbox (real-Seatbelt probes, `test.skipIf(seatbeltSkip !== null)`);
  - a credential printed by a gate reaches the coordinator redacted.

## Budget
#513's budget was split; this slice's is about 450 source lines plus tests.

## Out of scope
- Bonjour discovery, availability rules (AC power, idle) and a Workers page in the UI: the next slice.
- Whole-run workers, workers that update themselves, and waking sleeping machines.
- Linux workers (they need their own confinement).
- Model logins on workers.



Closes #547

One attempt can stay leased forever while its requests retry
A gate that leaves an unreadable directory stops the worker loop
Each lease poll sweeps every job once per held job
Worker caches keep every job's temporary bundle refs
Results may reorder the requested checks

## Why
Limitless has thorough documentation in the repository: README, docs/GUIDE.md, docs/OPERATIONS.md, docs/ARCHITECTURE.md and docs/EVALS.md. ## Change
1. **Site source and build.**
   - `site/` holds the landing page, its stylesheet and the page template.
   - `scripts/build-site.ts` renders the site into a gitignored output directory; biome and tsc must ignore it too.
   - Project Pages serve under `/limitless/`, so every URL is relative.
   - Keep it plain: static HTML and CSS, with no client framework and no third-party scripts or fonts.
2. **Docs are rendered, never copied.** At build time, render README.md, docs/GUIDE.md, docs/OPERATIONS.md, docs/ARCHITECTURE.md and docs/EVALS.md into pages, with a sidebar and an in-page table of contents. Exclude docs/PLAN.md, docs/BACKLOG.md, docs/test-performance.md and docs/research/.
   - Rewrite relative `X.md` and `X.md#anchor` links to the generated pages.
   - Rewrite links into the source tree (`src/…`, `scripts/…`, `test/…`) to GitHub blob URLs on main.
   - Heading anchors must match GitHub's slugs, so existing `#anchor` links keep working.
   - For Markdown rendering, first check what Bun (pinned in .github/workflows/ci.yml) provides. If a package is needed, add at most one devDependency, pinned to an exact version.
3. **Landing page.** In short sections:
   - what Limitless is: a personal software factory that takes a request through a deterministic pipeline with models working inside stages;
   - how a run works;
   - its main features, each with a screenshot;
   - links into the docs for installation, configuration and usage.
   Every claim must come from the docs as they are on main. Don't advertise unmerged work (for example worker gate jobs, #547). Say macOS where the docs require it.
4. **Screenshots from demo data only.** The private-strings check reads text, not pixels, so a screenshot must never show the owner's setup.
   - Add `scripts/site-screenshots.ts`, a manual script, not a test. It starts a daemon on loopback with a temporary home and the fake harness (src/harness/fake.ts).

   - Use a concurrency group for Pages.
6. Add a short "Website" note to docs/OPERATIONS.md: how to build and preview the site locally, how to regenerate screenshots, and that the repository's Pages source must be set to GitHub Actions.

- Build the site into a temporary directory and assert that every internal link and anchor resolves, and that every screenshot the landing page references exists.
- Assert that the excluded docs are absent from the output.
- Assert that a rendered doc's relative link to another doc and to a source file are rewritten as described.

- Analytics, cookies, tracking, or external fonts and scripts.
- Regenerating screenshots in CI.
- Rewriting the docs' content, beyond fixing links the build reports as broken.
- Enabling Pages in the repository settings (the owner does that).

About 600 lines, excluding the generated PNGs: site HTML and CSS, the build script, the screenshot script, the workflow and the test.

# Land checks: retry failing test files once before blocking

## Why
A land check runs the base commit's gates once (`LandQueue.checks`, src/land/queue.ts) and blocks on any failure. On 2026-10-16, load timeouts in known-flaky tests (#556) blocked five landings: lands 73, 75, 77, 80 and 81. Each one re-queued with no code change and waited hours for the single gate slot again. Factory gates already retry failing test files (#548); land checks don't.

Matt decided (2026-10-16): a land check re-runs only the failing test files once before blocking. A pass on that retry lands, recorded as flaky rather than as a clean pass. GitHub CI on the merged head still runs the full suite and must pass before the merge, as it does today, so that is the full-suite confirmation.

## Change
1. When a land check fails, retry only a check that ran and reported failed test files. That is a non-setup check that failed with a nonzero exit code, didn't time out as a whole, isn't a confinement failure, and has `failedFiles`. Retry it once with the base commit's `retry_files` command, the same targeted mechanism `retryFailures` in src/gates/run.ts uses: the same quoting, `validRetryFiles`, and slot rules for small retries. Reuse that code (export a targeted-only helper or add an option) rather than adding a second implementation.
2. If every retried check passes, continue landing:
   - Write the first failure and the retry to the land log.
   - Record the outcome on the land entry, for example the reason text `flaky: <check> (<files>)` kept after it lands.
   - Emit a warn-level event so the orchestrator sees a flaky landing.
3. Block exactly as today when:
   - setup fails;
   - lint, typecheck or another check fails without failed files;
   - the targeted retry fails or times out;
   - the base config has no usable `retry_files`;
   - anything reports a confinement failure. A confinement failure is never retried into a pass.
4. One retry layer, one attempt. No full-suite retry here (CI covers it), and no loop.

## Tests (fake gate runner, no network)
- A test check that fails with failed files and passes on the targeted retry lands. Its log and entry show the flake, and the retry command matches the base config's `retry_files`.
- A targeted retry that fails again blocks with today's message.
- Setup failure, a failing check without failed files, a whole-check timeout, a confinement failure, and a base config without `retry_files` each block with no retry.
- The retry uses the base commit's config even when the PR changes `retry_files` (trust boundary).
- A restart during the retry resumes the land from `checking` without landing on the strength of the unfinished retry.

## Out of scope
- Fixing the flaky tests themselves (#556), the gate-slot ordering (#569), and retries in run gates (#548).

## Budget
About 50 source lines plus tests.

Closes #571

defects.summary: A land retry must require complete failure attribution; otherwise it can land a suite that also failed elsewhere
Normalize the flaky diagnostic before redacting

# Land queue: a restart after GitHub merged can re-issue the merge

Found in #520's review; it predates that PR (same path on main).

## What happens
GitHub completes the merge, and the daemon restarts before the queue records it. On resume, `observe()` can return the retained `OPEN`, green snapshot for the pushed SHA without fetching again. `awaitCi()` then returns green (`src/land/queue.ts`, around line 480), and the queue calls `mergePullRequest()` again.

`mergePullRequest` (`src/git/repos.ts`, around lines 1244–1272) starts with `unsure = false` and reads only the title, body and head. It then issues `gh pr merge` without checking whether the PR has already merged. For a merged PR that command fails, so a PR that did land can end up blocked as "merge failed" until reconciliation corrects the run.

AGENTS.md requires that completed side effects never repeat after a restart.

## Change
- Before re-issuing a merge on resume (or whenever the entry was already `merging`), take a fresh merge-state observation from GitHub. If the PR has merged, record the landing, verifying that the merged head is the pushed SHA.
- Make `mergePullRequest` treat an already-merged PR at the expected head as success.

## Acceptance
A test fails on today's code:
1. Stop the queue after the merge command succeeded but before the record.
2. Keep a stale green snapshot.
3. Restart.

The entry lands without a second merge command.

Closes #521

Gates: a baseline confinement failure blocks every candidate, even passing confined ones

## Why
`compareGates` in src/gates/run.ts (around line 344) sets `verdict = "confinement_error"` when either the candidate's result or the baseline's counterpart fails confinement, and that verdict always blocks. So a baseline whose check output was classified as a confinement failure blocks every candidate for that check, including candidates that ran confined and passed.

It happened on #578 tonight. The round's baseline (the PR's previous head merged with main) failed tests whose fallback path printed the sandbox-apply failure literal, so the baseline's `test` check counted as a confinement failure. All five candidates in each of review rounds 2 and 3 then passed `test` on the LAN worker (`ok`, exit 0, `confinementError: false`), yet each was reported as "CONFINEMENT ERROR (sandbox launch failed)". Both rounds ended `needs_human` after five implementation attempts each, with nothing the implementer could change to pass.

## Change
A confinement failure in the baseline means the baseline result for that check is unusable, not that the candidate's confinement failed:
- candidate confinement failure: `confinement_error`, blocking (unchanged);
- baseline confinement failure and a confined candidate that passed: treat the baseline as missing for that check (the candidate's own passing, confined run stands);
- baseline confinement failure and a failing candidate: blocking, with a reason that says the baseline couldn't be compared (not a candidate confinement error), so the feedback doesn't send implementers chasing sandbox problems.

Keep the fail-closed rule for the candidate's own confinement.

## Tests
- A passing confined candidate against a baseline with a confinement failure doesn't block.
- A failing candidate against that baseline blocks with the "baseline couldn't be compared" reason.
- A candidate confinement failure still blocks as today.

## Out of scope
- The confinement-literal classification itself.

## Budget
About 20 source lines plus tests.

Closes #589

input.prompt:
Land queue: a worker that lost its claim can still write outcomes or merge

## Why
Found in #584's review; it predates that PR (the same paths on main).

A land worker keeps its claim with a heartbeat every `CLAIM_STALE_MS / 3` (`LandQueue.process`, src/land/queue.ts), and a failed heartbeat aborts the worker's signal. Between losing the claim and the next heartbeat, the old worker can still act on results it is awaiting:
- a `mergePullRequest` result that arrives after another owner reclaimed the entry: success moves the newer claim's entry to `landed`, failure moves it to `blocked` (`landed()` → `finish()` checks only that the entry is active, not who owns the claim);
- a resumed entry's CI response that arrives after a reclaim: the old worker can go on to issue the merge command.

Reproduction with the existing fake-gh/store helpers: defer `mergePullRequest`'s result, reclaim the entry with `store.claimLandEntry(<repo>, 30000, "new-owner", now + 31000)`, then release the result before the old worker's next heartbeat.

AGENTS.md "Check-then-act across an await" requires re-reading state after an await and making the write conditional.

## Change
After every await in the land path that precedes a side effect or an outcome write (CI wait, merge, push, the fresh merge-state lookup), confirm that this worker still owns the claim, synchronously in the same transaction as the write. A worker that lost the claim writes nothing and issues no merge or push.

## Tests (fake gh and store; no network)
- A deferred successful merge result released after a reclaim leaves the newer claim's state unchanged.
- A deferred failed merge result released after a reclaim leaves it unchanged.
- A deferred CI response released after a reclaim issues no merge command.

## Out of scope
- Changing the heartbeat interval or the claim lease length.

## Budget
About 30 source lines plus tests.

Closes #585

Claim-loss cleanup can delete the replacement worker's checkout

input.prompt:
Delivery: a resumed run whose base advanced twice is refused after a valid second factory merge

## What's wrong
Delivery refuses a resumed run whose base advanced twice. Found while vetting #467 for the fresh review clean set (#542). Both adjudicators reproduced it independently at #467's head (261559d), and it passed at its base (1aa4f2b). Keep "Act on the exact commit you checked": the accepted HEAD is the newest validated and gated merge, pinned when pushing.

## Tests
- Reproduce on main first: kill after the clean merge is persisted and before the push, advance the base again, then resume. Today that ends needs_human; after the fix it delivers M2.

About 30 source lines plus tests.

input.prompt:

## What's wrong
If the daemon dies while it is cleaning up an invocation's marked processes, nothing recovers the processes that cleanup hadn't finished with. A resumed run doesn't notice them.

Found while reviewing #561 (#537), which changes the cleanup to freeze and then kill. Reproduction (Codex, temporary test): a real runProcess invocation left a sleeper behind. This predates #561. Before it, the same crash left the processes running, which is worse: they could keep writing to the checkout. With #561 they are stopped, but they are still never cleaned up. The claimed set and its birth identities live only in memory.

When a run resumes, or the daemon starts, finish any recorded cleanup. Kill a recorded member only if its birth identity still matches, and refuse with a clear reason if confirmation fails, as cleanup already does. A resumed invocation must not start in a checkout whose previous cleanup is unresolved.

- Kill the cleanup process between freeze and kill, then resume. The stopped member is killed, identity-checked, before the next step runs.
- A recorded PID whose identity changed (reused) is never signalled.

## Budget
About 40 source lines plus tests.

Closes #562

input.prompt:

## What happened
`forgotten local execution stops before replacement (sha)` in `test/gate-executor.test.ts` failed once on Linux CI, on #563, a catalog-strings-only change. Main passes.

```
773 |           expect(() => process.kill(pid, 0)).toThrow();
error: expect(received).toThrow()
Received function did not throw
```

## Why (likely)
The test checks that a forgotten execution's `sleep 900` is gone by asserting `process.kill(pid, 0)` throws, right before the replacement starts and after each result. On Linux, a killed child stays in the process table as a zombie until its parent reaps it, and `kill(pid, 0)` on a zombie succeeds. The assertion therefore races the reap, and on a slow runner it can see the zombie. This is test flakiness. Nothing shows the cleanup itself leaving a live process, but the fix must confirm that.

## Change
- Make the test assert that the process is gone or a zombie, not merely that `kill(pid, 0)` fails. For example:
  - on Linux, read `/proc/<pid>/stat` and accept state `Z`, or a missing entry;
  - on macOS, use the existing process inspection.
- Alternatively, wait for the stop's own exit confirmation before asserting.
- Keep the assertion strict about a running (non-zombie) process.
- Check the other `process.kill(pid, 0)` "is gone" assertions in the test files for the same race.

## Acceptance
- The test still fails if cleanup leaves the process running. Show this by disabling the stop in a temporary probe.
- The test passes on Linux CI and macOS.

## Budget
Test-only. A few lines.

Closes #564

input.prompt:
CI: a hung test run leaves no log; stop it inside the step so the log is kept

## Problem
On 2026-10-08, two CI runs on Linux hung until the job's `timeout-minutes: 25` cancelled them (run 37725010065 on #408 at b3386bf, and run 37725905014 on #415 at 2e75ecc, about 15 minutes apart). A rerun of each passed in about 9 minutes, so something in the suite hangs intermittently on Linux.

Neither run left a log. When GitHub cancels a job at its timeout, the job log is not uploaded (the logs API returns `BlobNotFound`), so there is no way to see which test or process hung. The CI classifier then sees a cancelled run, not a failure with output.

## Change
1. `.github/workflows/ci.yml`: stop the check inside the step, a few minutes before the job timeout, so that the step fails and its log is kept. For example, run it under `timeout --signal=TERM --kill-after=30s 20m`, and before the kill, print what is still running: the process tree below the runner, and the test file bun was in. Keep `timeout-minutes` as the outer limit.
2. Make the hang identifiable from that log. If bun's own output doesn't show the active test file when it is stopped, print a marker as each test file starts, through the cheapest mechanism bun supports in CI only. Don't change local or factory test output.
3. Once a hang has been captured, fix its cause in a follow-up. This issue only has to make it visible.

## Tests
- A workflow-level check is enough: the step's command is a real `timeout` wrapper whose limit is below `timeout-minutes`. If any helper script is added, test it with a command that sleeps past a short limit: it must exit non-zero, print the process tree, and stop its children.

## Budget
About 20 lines in the workflow and any helper script.

## Out of scope
- Raising `timeout-minutes`.
- Retrying in CI.

input.prompt:
Invocation cleanup: a daemon crash mid-cleanup leaves descendants that a resumed run never recovers

## Scope (re-scoped 2026-10-19)
A first attempt (#624) didn't converge after three review rounds. It changed `processBirth`'s zombie semantics, and each later round found a new reaping race in the macOS leader inspection. Build the smaller change below; the original description further down is background.

**Change**
1. Before signalling any member during invocation cleanup, persist an ownership record: run, invocation, checkout directory, PID, birth identity and boot identity. The boot identity is `/proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id` on Linux and `kern.bootsessionuuid` on macOS; `kern.boottime` moves when the clock is set, so don't use it. Delete an invocation's records once its cleanup completes.
2. Recover recorded cleanups when a run resumes and before a run's next command in its own checkout. At daemon start, recover in the background after the HTTP server is up, so health isn't delayed. Recovery retires a record from another boot without signalling it, SIGKILLs every member whose birth identity still matches, then waits for all of them under one deadline, using its own liveness check that treats a zombie or a missing process as stopped. If confirmation fails, refuse with a clear reason, as cleanup already does.
3. Gate a run's commands only on that run's own records, or on records whose directory is inside the run's own checkout; shared factory directories (for example the repository cache) must not link runs. A missing checkout means no other run's records match, and the run's own records are still recovered (don't throw on a missing path).
4. In the cleanup error path, the live direct child (its ChildProcess handle has no exit or signal yet) is always SIGKILLed, even if recording it or inspecting it fails; keep those failures in the termination error.

**Don't change** `processBirth`, `captureDarwinInvocationLeader` or the live cleanup's process inspection. Rediscovering processes an interrupted sweep never recorded is #625.

**Compatibility** New table only (`process_cleanups`); the previous release ignores it.

**Tests**
- Kill the cleanup between freeze and kill, then resume: the stopped member is killed, identity-checked, before the next step runs.
- A recorded PID whose identity changed (reused), or a record from another boot, is never signalled.
- A cleanup error with inspection unavailable still kills the live direct child.
- Another run's unresolved record in a shared directory doesn't block or fail this run; a missing checkout doesn't fail recovery.

**Budget** About 120 source lines plus tests. Write scratch output under `$TMPDIR` only (AGENTS.md).

---

## What's wrong
If the daemon dies while it is cleaning up an invocation's marked processes, nothing recovers the processes that cleanup hadn't finished with. A resumed run doesn't notice them.

Found while reviewing #561 (#537), which changes the cleanup to freeze and then kill. Reproduction (Codex, temporary test): a real runProcess invocation left a sleeper behind. Inspection was paused after the sweep's SIGSTOP, and the owned supervisor was then killed. A fresh runProcess in the same directory returned exit code 0, while the previous sleeper stayed in state T.

This predates #561. Before it, the same crash left the processes running, which is worse: they could keep writing to the checkout. With #561 they are stopped, but they are still never cleaned up. The claimed set and its birth identities live only in memory.

## Change
Before signalling any process, persist the cleanup's ownership record: the run, the invocation, the claimed PIDs and their birth identities. When a run resumes, or the daemon starts, finish any recorded cleanup. Kill a recorded member only if its birth identity still matches, and refuse with a clear reason if confirmation fails, as cleanup already does. A resumed invocation must not start in a checkout whose previous cleanup is unresolved.

## Tests
- Kill the cleanup process between freeze and kill, then resume. The stopped member is killed, identity-checked, before the next step runs.
- A recorded PID whose identity changed (reused) is never signalled.

## Budget
About 40 source lines plus tests.

Closes #562

The real boot-identity reader is never exercised

input.prompt:
Cleanup recovery: rediscover marked processes an interrupted sweep never recorded

## Scope note (2026-10-19)
Recovery landed in #641 (not #624, which was closed): records live in `process_cleanups`, recovery uses its own zombie-aware liveness check, and a per-invocation lock serializes live cleanup and recovery. Build rediscovery on that. As in #562's re-scope, don't change `processBirth`, `captureDarwinInvocationLeader` or the live cleanup's process inspection; persist what discovery needs (marker, canonical directories) with the existing record and reuse the existing discovery code from recovery.

## What's wrong
Crash recovery of an invocation's cleanup (#562, PR #641) finishes only the members the interrupted sweep had already recorded. Live cleanup rescans after freezing, because a process tree keeps forking while it is being stopped. If the daemon dies mid-sweep, any process that a not-yet-frozen member forked after the last scan, or a sibling the sweep hadn't claimed yet, has no record. Recovery kills the recorded members, deletes the rows, and lets the next command start while those processes keep running in the checkout.

Found while reviewing #624 (Codex review). The window is the crash landing inside an active sweep of a growing tree, so it is rare, but the result is the state #562 set out to remove.

## Change
Persist what live cleanup uses to find an invocation's processes (the invocation marker and its canonical directories) with the ownership record. Before completing a recovered cleanup, run the same discovery: claim and record any newly found member (with its birth identity) before signalling it, and repeat until a scan finds nothing new, as live cleanup does. Keep the existing rules: never signal a process whose identity can't be confirmed, refuse with a clear reason when discovery is unavailable, and don't complete the record until the invocation is quiescent.

## Tests
- Interrupt a sweep after it froze a parent that then forked an unrecorded child; resume: the child is found, recorded and killed before the next command runs.
- Discovery unavailable during recovery: the record stays unresolved and the run refuses with a clear reason.

## Out of scope
Changing live cleanup.

## Budget
About 40 source lines plus tests.

Closes #625

input.prompt:
Gate substitution: accept skipped tests the base commit's baseline also skipped

## What's wrong
When a verifier marks a criterion such as "existing test suites still pass" as blocked by its sandbox, verify can substitute the factory's own gate result for it (`applyGateEvidence` in src/pipeline/gate-evidence.ts). Substitution refuses whenever any candidate gate check has `testCoverage.skippedFiles`, with "candidate gate checks did not all pass cleanly without retries or skipped tests".

This repository's suite always has skipped files inside confined gates: tests that need real Seatbelt use `test.skipIf(seatbeltSkip !== null)` and skip there by design (AGENTS.md, "Isolation"). So substitution can never apply here, and every run whose holdout or criteria include "the existing tests pass" ends as needs_human, even when every test that ran passed. Since 2026-10-14 this was the stated reason for about 20 of 49 needs_human runs (for example #644's run: test gate 4573 passed, 0 failed, 10 skipped files that the base commit's baseline also skipped).

## Change
Let substitution accept skipped tests that are inherited from the base commit, and nothing else:
- Record the identities of skipped tests (file plus test name, from Bun's `(skip)`/`(todo)` lines) in the gate result's test coverage, bounded in count and length like the existing coverage fields. Redact them like other gate output.
- In `passed()` (gate-evidence.ts), a check with skipped tests still qualifies only if the run's baseline (`ctx.state.baseline`, the same check name and command at the base commit) recorded skipped-test identities and every candidate skipped test appears in that baseline set. Pass the baseline in alongside the gate evidence; take it from factory records only.
- Refuse exactly as today when the baseline is missing, has no recorded identities (results from an older release), comes from a different command, or the candidate has any skipped test the baseline didn't have. A `(fail)` line still disqualifies the check, as do retries (`firstAttempt`), timeouts, confinement failures and incomplete output. The citation should say how many inherited skips there were.

Don't change what counts as a passing gate, a retry or a flaky result anywhere else.

## Compatibility
`testCoverage` is part of the worker protocol (src/workers/protocol.ts, `.strict()` schemas). Add the new field as optional. An older coordinator receiving it from a newer worker would reject the result, so check whether that can happen (workers follow the coordinator's release since #633), and note it in the PR.

## Tests
- A candidate whose skipped tests are a subset of the baseline's gets substitution; the citation counts the inherited skips.
- A candidate with one skipped test the baseline didn't have is refused; so is a missing baseline, a baseline without identities, and a `(fail)` line.
- Parsing records skipped-test identities from real Bun output lines (inline fixture).

## Budget
About 50 source lines plus tests.

Closes #646

defects.summary: Skipped-test identities come from console rows that Bun doesn't reliably print or attribute
Duplicate skipped-test identities are merged, so a new duplicate skip counts as inherited
The baseline may come from a different base commit than the one the candidate was merged with
Skipped tests in files the candidate changed count as inherited
Credential redaction can make two different test names compare equal
The refusal reason no longer says why skips were refused

input.prompt:
Redaction: decode filenames before matching credentials and private entries (audit findings, base64)

## What's wrong
Filenames in factory diagnostics are redacted only literally in two places, so an encoded secret in a path can be stored and shown:

1. **Audit findings.** `auditDiff` (src/gates/audit.ts) normalizes a finding's `file`, then checks it with `privateMatches` against the private entries only. Credentials are removed by `redactGateOutput`, which matches registered credentials literally. A filename containing a percent-encoded registered credential, or an HTML-encoded private entry (`privateMatches` doesn't decode HTML), survives into persisted audit findings, events and the implementer's next-round feedback. This applies to every audit rule that names a file, not just the scratch-output rules #640 added.
2. **Base64.** The publication decoder in src/gates/private.ts has no base64 support. A base64-encoded credential is not caught in published content, and #640's refusal diagnosis prints such a filename unchanged.

Found while verifying #640 (Codex review); both predate it.

## Change
- Audit: check each finding's normalized filename with the same decoding the publication check uses, against private entries and registered credentials, and replace it with `[redacted filename]` on a match. Treat the detail text the same way.
- Decide whether the publication check should recognise base64 runs that decode to a registered credential or a private entry (decoding only runs long enough to hold one, to keep false positives low), and apply that decision to the filename checks too. Document the decision if base64 stays out of scope.

## Tests
- An added file whose name holds a percent-encoded registered credential produces an audit finding with `[redacted filename]`, in persisted findings and in retry feedback.
- The same for an HTML-encoded private entry.
- Base64: per the decision above.

## Budget
About 30 source lines plus tests.

Closes #642

input.prompt:
Landing queue follow-ups: deploy when idle, and a land list in the UI

Follow-up from #352, parts 6 and 7, which weren't built when the landing queue shipped (#388).

## Change
1. **Deploy when idle (self-hosting only).** With `[deploy] after_land = "when_idle"`, the daemon deploys once the landing queue has no active entry and no run is active. It is off by default, and a new optional config key with a default is fine for an older release (say so next to the key in the docs). Today the orchestrator does this with a script that polls `land_entries`.
   - Reuse `limitless deploy`'s path: checks, smoke, drain and restart with rollback.
   - Deploy only a main that changed since the running release.
   - A failed deploy blocks further automatic deploys until the next landing. The feed says why.
2. **A land list in the UI.** Show the queue's entries (state, PR, approved SHA, reason, log link), newest first, with a cancel action for active entries. It reads `/api/land`. Follow the UI rules in AGENTS.md: the newest response wins, and refresh after a mutation.

- With `after_land = "when_idle"` and a fake deploy hook: a landing followed by an idle queue deploys once. An active run delays it. A second landing during the delay still deploys only once.
- With the key unset, nothing deploys.
- The UI list renders entries and refreshes after a cancel.

## Out of scope
Deploying for repositories other than the daemon's own.

Closes #470

input.prompt:
Run review and verify in parallel

## Scope (refreshed 2026-10-20 for the current pipeline)
In a round of the standard and deep profiles, `oneRound` (src/pipeline/engine.ts) runs review, then, only if review approves, waits for the holdout scenarios, builds the preview (when the change needs one) and runs verify. Review and verify are both read-only, work from the same committed HEAD, and neither needs the other's output, but verify always waits for review. Run them concurrently, with the outcome unchanged.

## Change
1. **Order.** After gates and audit pass, settle everything that touches the worktree first: wait for the holdout scenarios and run the preview stage (its setup and build, #644) when one is needed. Then start the review stage and the verify stage together. Nothing may change the worktree (verify's `discardChanges`, `resetTo`, preview setup) while either stage runs; verify's post-invocation discard moves to after both have settled.
2. **One decision point.** Neither branch writes `ctx.state.feedback` or decides the round. Wait for both with `Promise.allSettled`, then decide deterministically:
   - review requests changes: the round's feedback is the review feedback, followed by a separate `### Acceptance criteria not yet met (verify)` section listing verify's unmet criteria, if any. Panel limits (`PANEL_REVIEWS`) and the needs_human path behave exactly as today;
   - review approves: the outcome is exactly today's verify outcome, including the blocked-only verify retry on another model, which runs after both have settled;
   - an error in either branch (holdout failure, `Holdout scenarios are unavailable`, `Commit changed during verification`, cancellation) still lets the other branch settle (no orphaned invocation, no stage row left `running`) before it propagates.
   The final state and feedback must not depend on which stage finishes first.
3. **Paths that stay sequential.** Quick profile (no verify), verify-change flow, review-resolution rounds and conflict rounds keep today's order.
4. **Resume.** Review results are cached per round and HEAD (`completedChecks`); verify isn't. A restart after review finished reuses review only if HEAD is unchanged and reruns verify. `ctx.run.stage` holds one name; set it to `review` while both run (display only).

## Out of scope
No change to verdict logic, routing, vendor exclusion, panel rules, holdout authoring or gate evidence.

## Tests (fake harness)
- Both invocations start before either finishes (controllable fakes, overlapping timestamps).
- Review blocks and verify passes: review feedback only. Review approves and verify fails: verify feedback. Both fail: review feedback plus the verify section.
- Each of those runs in both finish orders and produces identical state and feedback.
- An error in verify while review is in flight: review settles, then the error propagates; no stage row left running.
- No worktree change happens while review runs (assert discard/reset/preview timing against the review invocation).
- A restart after review finished reuses it at the same HEAD and reruns verify; at a different HEAD it reruns both.
- Quick, verify-change and resolution rounds are unchanged.

## Budget
About 120 changed source lines plus tests. Earlier attempts at large engine changes looped in review; keep it tight.

Closes #82

defects.summary: A verify-side failure now overrides a review that requested changes
A retry recorded at an older SHA now consumes the current SHA's retry
A resumed retry can rerun the verifier that just blocked

input.prompt:
Issue #682: CI failure signature and excerpt should come from the failing lines

## Problem
`ciSignature` in `src/integrations/ci-classifier.ts` picks the first log line matching `/timed out after|##\[error\]|\b(?:error|fail(?:ed|ure)?)\b/i` anywhere in the line. In a Bun log that is usually a *passing* test whose name contains "failure" or "error". On #676 the signature line was `(pass) an answering endpoint rejection never falls back, and socket failure rechecks HTTP`, although the failing test was `(fail) real Bun bail blocks targeted land retry …`. The `emit` excerpt is the first 2,000 characters of the whole job log, which is the runner-provisioning header (runner version, image, region).

Both go to the CI-fix round: `startRoundTrigger` puts the trigger's `check`, `line` and `excerpt` in the fix round's request, and the round's PR comment quotes `line`. A fix round therefore gets a passing test's name and runner boilerplate instead of the failure. The signature also names the record in `ci_failures` for a PR, commit and check, so different failures on one commit get the same name.

## Requirements
- Choose the signature line from failure-shaped lines only, parsed by structure: the same line-start patterns `securityFailure` already uses (`(fail)`, `FAIL`/`FAILED`, `✗ ✕ × ● ❌`, `--- FAIL:`, `not ok`, `##[error]`, `error:`), plus the timeout diagnostics. Keep today's fallback when no line matches.
- Take the excerpt from the failure region: the lines around the chosen signature line, still bounded to 2,000 characters, redacted before truncation as now.
- One implementation for both call sites that build a signature from a log (the inspection path and rerun resolution).
- Records written by the previous release still resolve. A pending rerun recorded under an old signature must not be requested again or lost after the deploy; the rerun claim is also matched by job, so check that path with a test.
- Tests built from a short inline Bun log: a passing test whose name contains "failure" appears before a real `(fail)` line, and the signature and excerpt name the real failure. Also a GitHub Actions log with the runner header first.

## Out of scope
The security classification, the transient/timeout rules, which failures trigger reruns, and the test-title annotation problem (filed separately).

Budget: about 80 lines including tests.

Closes #682

defects.summary: Redacting the whole job log twice adds over half a second of event-loop blocking per inspection

input.prompt:
Issue #681: Test titles create a security error annotation on every CI run

## Problem
`test/ci-classifier.test.ts` runs `test.each(securityRecords)("a failing security record blocks reruns and the ledger: %s", …)`, so each raw record is printed in a test title. One record is `##[error]security tests failed`. The GitHub Actions runner parses a legacy `##[…]` command anywhere in a line, not only at its start. So every CI run of this repository, passing or failing, gets a real error annotation reading "security tests failed [50.25ms]". The job log shows it as `##[error]security tests failed [50.25ms]` (see https://github.com/MattFlower/limitless/actions/runs/39530195892).

`src/integrations/ci-classifier.ts` treats an `##[error]` line that mentions security as a security failure, correctly and fail-closed. As a result, every failing CI run of this repository since a9221aa (2026-10-06) has been classified unsafe: no rerun of transient failures, no `ci_failures` record and no CI-fix trigger. The factory raised 39 `ci.needs_fix` items in that time, but recorded 2 CI failures and 1 fix trigger.

## Requirements
- No test title or printed string in the suite contains a runner command: `##[` anywhere in a line, or `::error`, `::warning`, `::notice`, `::group` and the like at the start of a line. Give the `test.each` cases labels instead of the raw records. The records themselves stay as they are.
- Keep the classifier unchanged. A real `##[error]` line about security must still block reruns.
- Add a line to `test/AGENTS.md` next to the existing `sandbox_apply` warning in AGENTS.md: Actions parses `##[…]` anywhere in a line of the job log, so test titles and printed output must not contain runner commands.
- Test: a guard test that fails when a test title in `test/ci-classifier.test.ts` would contain `##[`. Optional if a simpler check covers it.

## Out of scope
Classifier logic, signature or excerpt selection (filed separately), other test files unless they print runner commands too (check with `grep -rn '##\[' test/`).

Budget: about 20 lines.

Closes #681

input.prompt:
Issue #709: Admin sampling profile to find the daemon's event-loop stall sources

## Problem
#690's stall reporter (shipped in #700) shows the daemon's event loop still stalling in production: 51 stalls over 2.5 hours after a restart, median 4.9 s, longest 30 s. In every report the instrumented activities (`credentials.redact`, `credentials.data`, `gates.redact`, `store.event`) add up to under 10 ms, so the time goes to code the reporter doesn't cover.

A 4-minute native stack sample that caught four stalls (about 21 s in total) found the daemon's main thread running JIT-compiled JavaScript for about 36 s. It was not blocked in I/O (`sqlite3_step` accounts for about 0.6 s). The release Bun binary is stripped, so a native sample can't name the JavaScript functions, and the next step of #690 (find and fix the top stall sources, with before and after numbers) needs those names.

`profile(callback, sampleIntervalMicroseconds)` from `bun:jsc` samples all JavaScript on the main thread while the callback's promise is pending, including timer, I/O and HTTP callbacks unrelated to the callback itself. Checked: with `profile(() => Bun.sleep(3000), 1000)` and a 300 ms busy `setInterval` callback, the callback got 1395 of 1397 samples, by name. It returns `{ functions, bytecodes, stackTraces }` as text.

## Requirements
- Add `POST /api/admin/profile` to `src/server/http.ts`, next to `/api/admin/drain` and `/api/admin/resume`, with the same loopback-only and authentication rules as the other admin routes. The body is `{ "seconds": number }`, from 0.2 to 120 with a default of 30. The route runs `profile(() => Bun.sleep(seconds * 1000), 1000)` and responds with JSON `{ seconds, functions, stackTraces }`. Each text field is passed through `redactCredentials` and capped at 64 KiB.
- Only one profile can run at a time. A second request while one is running gets HTTP 409 with a clear message. A failure inside the profiler responds with an error and leaves no profile marked as running.
- A test that starts a busy, uniquely named timer callback, calls the route with `seconds: 0.3`, and finds that name in `functions`. A second test asserts the 409 for a concurrent request. Keep both well under a second.
- Document the route in `docs/OPERATIONS.md` under Troubleshooting: what the "Event loop stall" log lines mean, how to call the route with the API token, and that a profile adds a little sampling overhead while it runs.

## Out of scope
Fixing the stall sources (a follow-up, once a production profile names them), changes to the stall reporter, the CLI, and the daemon's launchd job settings.

Budget: about 40 lines plus tests and the doc paragraph.

Part of #690.

Closes #709

defects.summary: Capping the raw stackTraces JSON keeps an arbitrary prefix and drops the source mapping

input.prompt:
Issue #703: Timeout classification and deploy retry polish after #700

## Problem
#700's final review found three edges in its changes, accepted at merge so deploys could be unblocked:

1. **A genuine timeout can be reported as an ordinary exit.** `runProcess` (`src/util/proc.ts`) now keeps `timedOut` and `idleTimedOut` only when the timeout shutdown actually killed a running direct child. A child that is still running when the deadline fires, but exits by itself while the shutdown is inspecting processes, is reported by its exit status. Reproduced with a 40 ms deadline: exit 7 became an ordinary `CommandError`, and exit 0 made `sh` succeed. That changes gate timeout reruns, harness `stuck` results and land-check outcomes in that window. The previous behaviour had the opposite error (a child that exited before the deadline was reported as timed out during event-loop stalls, #690), which is why #700 changed it.
2. **Health-body failures count as unanswered polls.** `unanswered()` in `src/cli/deploy-wait.ts` accepts raw transport error codes, including errors thrown by `response.json()` after the headers arrived. Reproduced: HTTP 200 with a body stream failing with `ECONNRESET` is retried, and near the drain deadline it resolves and logs "restarting".
3. **The rollback's resume retries permanent failures.** `requestAdmin(..., "resume")` retries everything except `DrainUnsupportedError`, so HTTP 401, invalid JSON or a missing acknowledgement cause 60 attempts over 120 s before the deploy reports the stranded scheduler.

- runProcess: classify by whether the child was still running when the deadline was reached, not by whether cleanup's kill was the one that ended it. If the runtime can't tell exit-before-deadline from exit-after-deadline when an event-loop stall delays both callbacks, keep #700's behaviour and document the trade-off in a comment. Don't reintroduce the false timeout for a child that exited before its deadline. Tests for both orders.
- deploy-wait: retry only failures that happened before a response arrived (connection errors, timeouts). Body or validation errors after headers fail the poll. Resume retries only connection errors and timeouts, so HTTP errors, invalid bodies and missing acknowledgements are reported immediately. Tests for each.

## Out of scope
The stall reporter, finding the stall sources.

Budget: about 40 lines plus tests.

Closes #703

Issue #707: Gate-output redaction: terminal sequences on top of the multi-pattern matcher

## Problem
#435 deferred four cases from #421 where terminal escape sequences around or inside a registered credential let part of it reach stored gate output, artifacts, events, feedback and prompts. #694 attempted them with a stateful parser over per-credential matching. It was closed after seven attempts: each round found a new leak, and it was 45 to 80 times slower than today's redactor. This issue redoes the terminal handling on top of the multi-pattern matcher from #706, under a strict budget.

## Design constraints
- **Built on #706.** Match through its automaton, so cost per byte stays independent of the number of registered credentials. No per-credential loops.
- **Fail closed on ambiguity.** Where a sequence's extent is ambiguous (a stray or incomplete `ESC [`, `ESC ]` or C1 introducer, an unterminated OSC, DCS, SOS, PM or APC string, a line break or another escape inside a string, or a string longer than the hold), the result must not depend on which reading is right. A credential found under any reasonable reading (raw text with only the control bytes removed, or the ECMA-48 stripped text) is redacted over its raw span. Dropping ambiguous control bytes from the stored output is acceptable.
- **Never swallow output.** An unterminated or malformed string sequence ends at a bound (a line break or the hold limit), and the held text is then emitted as visible and redacted, never discarded.
- **Independent of chunk boundaries.** The same bytes produce the same output at every split.
- **Bounded carry.** Held state is at most the longest credential variant plus a fixed amount, whatever the overlap pattern.
- Keep #421's single redaction point and its guarantees: redact before framing and truncation, and the confinement scan still sees raw output.

## Required tests
Each of these is a known leak or defect from #435 and from #694's reviews. Run each at every split position across two chunks.
1. A stray `ESC [`, `ESC ]` or C1 CSI immediately before a credential (it must not consume the first character), including when the credential itself also contains a sequence.
2. A DCS, a C1 OSC, and an OSC longer than the hold limit inside a credential.
3. A stray OSC before a line break, then an SGR inside the credential that follows (#694's final finding).
4. Two multiline terminal strings interrupting the same credential (#694 round 5).
5. An unterminated or malformed OSC or DCS followed by more output: the later output, including a credential in it, is still emitted and redacted, not swallowed.
6. A multiline terminal string over the hold limit, and a BEL terminator.
7. A credential registered while the stream is open, appearing after registration.
8. A periodic credential repeated through a large stream, asserting the held buffer's size.
9. Performance: 5 MB at 0 and 600 registered credentials, with before and after numbers in the PR (within about 2 times of #706's redactor).

Use synthetic credentials registered in the test, never real ones.

## Out of scope
Credentials split across stdout and stderr, or encoded by the program (base64, URL encoding; #335). Rows stored before #421.

Budget: about 150 source lines plus tests. If the design needs more, stop and say why in the report instead of growing it.

Closes #707

Issue #718: Holdout redaction rebuilds its patterns for every streamed agent string (main event-loop stall source)

## Problem
The production profile endpoint from #709 caught the main source of #690's event-loop stalls. In a 120 s profile on 2026-10-21 there were 13 stalls of 2–11 s. 92% of the stack samples that fit in the output were in holdout redaction on streamed agent output:

`redactHoldoutText` (src/pipeline/prompts.ts) < `redactOutput` (src/harness/types.ts:135) < `redactJsonLine` < `onStdoutLine` (src/harness/claude.ts:424) < `runProcess`'s line emitter

`redactJsonLine` calls the run's redactor once for every string value of every JSON event line. For a run with holdout scenarios, each call runs `privateHoldoutDetails`. That compiles a new `RegExp(holdoutBoundaryPattern(detail), "iu")` for every scenario field, sentence and syntax-shaped literal, and tests each one against `publicSources`. It then compiles one alternation regex over every detail and runs the replacement. All of that depends only on the holdout and `publicSources`, except for the literals collected from the value itself (`includeObservedLiterals`). A run with several long scenarios therefore spends seconds per burst of agent output, on the daemon's main thread.

Process scanning (`markedDarwinProcesses`/`predatesSpawn` under `stopMarkedProcesses`) came second, at 4.5%. It is out of scope here.

## Requirements
- Make `redactHoldoutText` cheap per call without changing its output. Compute the scenario-derived details once per (holdout, `publicSources`) pair, keyed by the holdout object's identity (for example a `WeakMap`), then by `publicSources`. Cache the boundary test for each literal against `publicSources`, and reuse the compiled replacement pattern whenever the detail set for a call is unchanged (always, when no observed literal adds a detail). Observed literals are still collected from each value as today.
- Output must be identical to the current implementation. Add a differential test that keeps a copy of today's function in the test file and compares both on a few hundred generated values against a holdout with several multi-sentence scenarios. The values should include scenario sentences, literals that appear and don't appear in `publicSources`, quoted strings, paths, flags and numbers.
- Measure at production size, as AGENTS.md now asks. Use a holdout with 8 scenarios of about 600 characters each, `publicSources` of about 20 KB, and 20,000 event-sized strings (100–400 characters, some containing scenario literals). Report the before and after totals and the worst single call in the PR. Put the benchmark in `scripts/benchmark-holdout-redaction.ts`; tests don't assert timings.
- Keep the precomputation scoped to one invocation, with no module-level cache that grows with every run's holdout. The streaming redactor is built once per invocation in `src/pipeline/context.ts` (around line 772), from `this.state.holdout` and the `publicSources` computed just above it. Building a precomputed redactor there (for example `holdoutRedactor(holdout, publicSources)`, returning `(value) => string`) and keeping `redactHoldoutText` as a thin wrapper for the one-off callers is the preferred shape; a `WeakMap` keyed by the holdout object is also acceptable.

## Out of scope
Process scanning cost, the stall reporter, credential redaction, and changing which details count as private.

Budget: about 40 source lines, plus the test and the benchmark script.

Part of #690.

Closes #718

defects.summary: Each call still compiles a combined regex over every detail, so the stall remains (1.06x faster)

Issue #728: Workers: agent-job routes on the worker listener

## Problem
Epic #165, slice S3 (plan and owner decisions on #165). #726 added the `agent_jobs` table and its lease transitions on `WorkerStore`, but workers have no way to lease an agent job or report on one. The owner decided that workers commit and push their own work to GitHub, and that a coordinator restart must not lose an in-flight session (durable re-attach, a later slice). So the coordinator needs routes for lease, checkout, events, result and failure, and events must persist rather than pass through an in-memory hand-off.

## Requirements
- **Lease.** `POST /worker/lease` (src/server/workers.ts) tries a gate lease first, exactly as today, then `leaseAgentJob`. The reply becomes `{ job, agentJob }`, where `agentJob` is `null` or `{ id, remainingMs, request }`. The request carries no coordinator filesystem paths. The existing `job` field and its behaviour are unchanged, so current workers keep working. Lockstep already restricts leases to same-release workers.
- **Routes.** All under `/worker/agent-jobs/:id/`. Each sits behind the existing bearer check and `holdsAgentJob(id, worker)`, and answers 409 to a worker that doesn't hold the job:
  - `GET bundle`: a git bundle of the job's `parent_sha` (and the base commit when the request names one), built with the same helper as the gate bundle route. Extract that helper rather than copying it.
  - `POST events`: a strict, bounded batch `{ seq, events }`, where `events` follows the existing agent event shape. Batches over 1 MiB are refused. Each batch is redacted with `redactCredentialData` and stored in a new table, `agent_job_events (job_id, seq, events, created_at)`, with primary key `(job_id, seq)`. A duplicate `seq` is acknowledged and ignored. Add the table in a new migration with explicit-column inserts. A later slice drains it into the run's event stream, which keeps events intact across a coordinator restart.
  - `POST result`: a strict schema covering the `AgentResult` fields (`status`, `finalText`, `structured`, `sessionId`, `usage`, `numTurns`, `costUsd`, `costEquivUsd`, `error`, `quota`, `modelCooldownMs`, `decline`, `confinement`), plus `{ parentSha, sha, branch }`.
    - `parentSha` must equal the job's `parent_sha`.
    - `sha` must be a full hex object id. It equals `parentSha` when the session changed nothing.
    - `branch` must be a valid branch name.
    - The route records the result with `completeAgentJob`. It does not fetch from GitHub; verifying the pushed commit is the coordinator executor's job in a later slice.
  - `POST failure`: `{ reason }`, which calls `failAgentJob`. The reason is sanitized as for gate jobs.
- Request size limits are checked per route. JSON routes stay within today's 2 MiB cap, and the events route refuses anything over 1 MiB.
- Nothing enqueues agent jobs in production yet, and no worker leases them yet.

## Tests (loopback TLS listener, as in test/workers.test.ts)
- Each new route returns 401 without a token and 409 for a worker that doesn't hold the job. An oversized events batch is refused.
- Lease order: a gate job wins over a queued agent job. An agent job is leased when no gate job is queued. The reply keeps `job` for current workers.
- Events: a malformed batch is refused, a duplicate `seq` is ignored, and a credential registered on the coordinator never reaches the stored events.
- Result: a mismatched parent, a malformed SHA and an invalid branch are each rejected, and a valid result moves the job to `done` with `result_sha`.
- A revoked token in the middle of a job gets 401.
- Store one production-sized event volume (for example 2,000 events in 10 batches) and report the timing in the PR.

## Out of scope
The worker client, enqueueing from runs, fetching and verifying pushed commits, draining events into runs, re-attach.

Budget: about 150 lines plus the migration and tests.

Part of #165.

Closes #728

Issue #733: Workers: run leased agent jobs and report events and results

## Problem
Epic #165, slice S4a (plan and owner decisions on #165). The coordinator can now queue and lease agent jobs (#726), and serves checkout bundles and accepts events, results and failures (#730). Workers don't act on agent jobs yet: `runWorker` (src/workers/client.ts) parses the lease reply with a schema that drops `agentJob`, and only gate jobs run. This slice makes a worker run a leased agent session and report its events and result. Committing and pushing the session's changes is the next slice (S4b), and recovering orphaned processes after a worker crash is S4c.

## Requirements
- **Request fields.** Extend `AgentJobRequest` (src/db/workers.ts) additively with what a session needs: `role`, `mode`, `systemAppend`, `jsonSchema`, `idleTimeoutMs`, `maxToolCalls`, `fast`, `privateSession`, `confineReads`, `slottedCommands` and `branch`. Include them in the lease reply's projection in src/server/workers.ts. The request still carries no coordinator filesystem paths and no credentials; enqueue already refuses those.
- **Shared runner.** Extract the tool-enabled branch of `invoke` (the `local` closure in src/pipeline/context.ts: `withScratch` → `withSlottedCommands` → harness) into a shared function, for example `runToolAgent` in src/pipeline/agent-executor.ts. `invoke` keeps its behaviour exactly, and the worker uses the same function.
- **Worker loop.**
  - Parse an optional `agentJob` in the lease reply.
  - Keep running agent jobs in their own map, so gate `freeSlots` is unaffected.
  - Report held agent job ids in the heartbeat and lease `jobs` lists, as gate jobs are.
  - The update drain before a self-update also waits for running agent jobs.
- **Checkout.** Fetch `GET /worker/agent-jobs/:id/bundle` and make a detached checkout at `parentSha` in the job's own scratch, verifying HEAD. Use the same steps as the gate job runner, extracted into a helper rather than copied.
- **Harness.** Pick the worker's local harness by `target.harness`, supporting `claude` and `codex`. Any other harness posts `failure` with "provider unavailable on worker". Run the session under the worker's confinement and read policy, as gate jobs do.
- **Test slots stay local.** Agent test commands (slotted commands) use the worker process's own in-process gate-slot pool, sized by the worker's configured gate slots. Pass no coordinator port, so the HTTP fallback can never reach the coordinator.
- **Events.**
  - Batch them: post when 250 ms have passed or 200 events have accumulated, whichever comes first, with a monotonic `seq`, through `POST events`.
  - Replace the worker's checkout and scratch paths with the placeholder `<worktree>` before posting.
  - Bodies already go through the client's redaction.
  - A rejected batch fails the job.
- **Result.**
  - Post `POST result` with the session's `AgentResult`, `parentSha`, `branch`, and `sha = parentSha`. Discard the checkout afterwards, since committing is S4b.
  - On a harness or checkout error, post `failure` with a sanitized reason.
- **Fencing.** If no heartbeat has succeeded for longer than one lease period, abort every running agent job, so a partitioned worker stops spending quota. A heartbeat reply that lists a held agent job as cancelled aborts that job.
- Nothing enqueues agent jobs in production yet, so this code stays idle until the switch slice (S5).

## Tests (fake harness, loopback TLS listener and the real worker loop, as in test/workers.test.ts)
- A queued agent job is leased, checked out at the parent and run, and its events arrive in `agent_job_events` in order with the paths replaced. The result moves the job to `done` with `result_sha` equal to the parent.
- A heartbeat cancellation aborts the running harness.
- An injected partition (heartbeats failing) aborts the job after one lease period.
- An unsupported harness posts a failure.
- Gate jobs keep running alongside an agent job, and gate `freeSlots` is unchanged by it.
- A self-update waits for a running agent job.
- `invoke` produces identical events and invocation rows through the extracted runner (an existing test, or a new one).

## Out of scope
Committing and pushing (S4b), worker-local process-cleanup recovery (S4c), enqueueing from runs (S5), re-attach (S6), capabilities (S7).

Budget: about 150 lines plus tests. If it can't fit, stop at the first seam that keeps everything working and say what's left in the report.

Part of #165.

Closes #733

Fencing fires up to one heartbeat interval after the lease has expired

Issue #735: Workers: per-job process scope and a local cleanup store

## Problem
Epic #165, slice S4c (plan on #165). It must land before S5, the switch that first enqueues agent jobs. Worker agent sessions (#734) run without the coordinator's per-job process scope or a durable cleanup store. In the review of #734, Codex injected a process-discovery failure while an agent-owned child was running. The worker posted "Invocation termination could not be confirmed", deleted the checkout and scratch, and continued without cleanup records, so descendants that may still be running can overlap a retried job. A worker crash also leaves orphaned CLI processes that keep spending quota, because the worker process has no store and `recoverProcessCleanups` never runs there.

## Requirements
- Run each worker job (agent sessions, and gate jobs if they have the same gap; check and say which) inside a per-job process scope, as the coordinator's engine does (`processScope` in src/util/proc.ts).
- Give the worker a local `Store` at `<data>/worker/worker.db`, protected with `protectDatabase`, and use it as the process-cleanup store. Run `recoverProcessCleanups` when the worker starts.
- When termination of a job's processes can't be confirmed (`ProcessTerminationError`), keep the job's checkout and scratch until termination is confirmed, either later or during recovery, and record the process identities durably. The job is still reported as failed.
- Tests:
  - an injected discovery failure keeps the directories and records the processes;
  - a simulated worker restart recovers and cleans them up;
  - a normal job still removes everything;
  - gate jobs are unaffected or fixed the same way.

## Out of scope
Enqueueing (S5), re-attach (S6), capabilities (S7).

Budget: about 80 lines plus tests.

Part of #165.

Closes #735

defects.summary: Restart deletes retained directories when no process identity was recorded
